title: Silicon carbide capacity (wafers & fabs)
scope: Substrate / boule / wafer / epi / captive fab throughput for SiC power. Not device design-wins (see field-sic Infineon/STM). Not burn-in equipment (see sic-burn-in.html AEHR/Cohu).
framing: Performance tracker scores are live (as of 2026-10-01). Six one-screen capacity scorecards under analysis/companies/. Gold at most two capacity names this pass; rainbow used only if capacity upside looks under-priced (none this pass). Not investment advice.

companies.name: Wolfspeed
companies.role: Vertical SiC materials + Mohawk Valley 200mm fab / JP materials center — capacity pure-play.
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Story is wafer/fab throughput and materials scale, not SST design-wins.
companies.caveats: Chapter 11 emergence Sep 2025; fresh-start accounting; Renesas equity; dilution/covenant overhang.
companies.rainbowReason: Post-Ch.11 equity and low Mohawk utilization; capacity not under-priced cleanly.

metrics.label: 200 mm fab readiness
metrics.note: Mohawk Valley is sole 200 mm device fab after Durham 150 mm close.

metrics.label: Utilization / ramp
metrics.note: Utilization still low-~20s%; underutilization losses persist into 2026.

metrics.label: Vertical integration
metrics.note: Substrate (Durham/JP) into captive 200 mm device fab — U.S. supply chain.

metrics.label: Balance sheet / Ch.11
metrics.note: Emerged Sep 2025; fresh-start accounting; $350M cash covenant; dilution overhang.

metrics.label: Customer concentration
metrics.note: Top customers dominate; Renesas equity + supply deal deepen single-buyer risk.

metrics.label: Valuation vs peers
metrics.note: Distressed multiple vs capacity footprint, but equity structure still messy.

companies.thesis: Wolfspeed is the clearest U.S. silicon carbide capacity story — boule/substrate into the Mohawk Valley 200 mm fab — but Chapter 11 emergence (Sep 2025), fresh-start accounting, Renesas equity, and still-low fab utilization mean the balance sheet and fill rate dominate the capacity thesis for now.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.role: Merchant SiC substrates and epitaxial wafers (incl. 200mm epi).
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Materials/epi supplier; does not compete as a power-device brand on the device field.
companies.caveats: Lasers/networking dilute SiC purity; EV wafer demand cyclical.
companies.rainbowReason: AI optics + SiC headlines already rerated the stock; capacity not under-priced.

metrics.label: 200 mm epi readiness
metrics.note: Shipping 200 mm n-type epi (from Sep 2024); thick epi to ~10 kV class.

metrics.label: Merchant materials share
metrics.note: DENSO / Mitsubishi Electric equity + long-term substrate/epi supply.

metrics.label: SiC revenue purity
metrics.note: Lasers and optical networking still dominate the equity story.

metrics.label: Customer diversification
metrics.note: Device OEMs as buyers; not captive-only to one auto line.

metrics.label: EV / wafer cyclicality
metrics.note: Wafer demand tied to EV and industrial power cycles.

metrics.label: Valuation vs peers
metrics.note: Elevated after AI optics / SiC headlines; capacity not free.

companies.thesis: Coherent sells merchant SiC epitaxial wafers — including 200 mm — so device makers can ramp without owning crystal growth. Thick epi aimed at multi-kilovolt AI-datacenter and industrial power is a capacity differentiator, but lasers/networking still dilute how pure the equity is to SiC wafers.
companies.street: Street leaning: Moderate Buy (MarketBeat consensus, 2026; targets lifted after Apr 2026 thick-epi news).

companies.name: onsemi
companies.role: Captive end-to-end SiC (boule → epi → fab), e.g. Hudson NH; Czech 200mm plans.
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Investment angle is captive capacity assurance; finished devices are secondary for this field.
companies.caveats: Also sells devices; Czech expansion timing/incentive uncertainty.
companies.rainbowReason: Captive SiC capacity is widely covered; utilization recovery already visible in numbers.

metrics.label: Captive vertical depth
metrics.note: Boule (Hudson) through epi and device fab — assurance-of-supply model.

metrics.label: 200 mm readiness
metrics.note: Czech Rožnov 200 mm end-to-end targeted commercial ~2027; EC aid approved.

metrics.label: Utilization / demand
metrics.note: Company utilization recovered ~68% YE2025 → ~83% by Aug 2026.

metrics.label: Customer / LTA base
metrics.note: Broad auto and industrial LTAs; not a single-buyer materials story.

metrics.label: Czech timing risk
metrics.note: Incentive and build timeline still execution-sensitive before 2027.

metrics.label: Balance sheet
metrics.note: Investment-grade scale; no restructuring overhang like pure-play peers.

companies.thesis: onsemi's SiC angle here is captive capacity — growing crystals in Hudson, NH and pushing a full-chain 200 mm hub in the Czech Republic — so auto and industrial customers get supply assurance without betting on a distressed materials pure-play. Finished MOSFETs matter commercially, but this field scores the fab/materials footprint.
companies.street: Street leaning: Moderate Buy (MarketBeat consensus, late Sep 2026).

companies.name: Resonac
companies.role: Independent SiC epitaxial-wafer specialist — merchant epi capacity.
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Epi/materials only; no MOSFET design-win narrative on this hub.
companies.caveats: Chemicals conglomerate mix; ADR liquidity; China substrate competition.
companies.rainbowReason: Epi quality is known; ADR friction and conglomerate mix limit under-priced capacity call.

metrics.label: Epi quality / share
metrics.note: Merchant epi specialist; long-cited share leader on defect metrics.

metrics.label: 200 mm epi ramp
metrics.note: 200 mm shipments underway; Yamagata building targeted Q3 2025 completion.

metrics.label: Independence (no device conflict)
metrics.note: Epi-only model attracts captive device makers as customers.

metrics.label: 300 mm R&D optionality
metrics.note: 300 mm substrate milestone Sep 2026 — still pre-commercial.

metrics.label: Conglomerate mix
metrics.note: Chemicals / materials group dilutes pure epi exposure.

metrics.label: ADR liquidity
metrics.note: OTC ADR thin vs TSE 4004; friction for U.S. accounts.

companies.thesis: Resonac is a merchant SiC epi specialist — it does not sell MOSFETs — so device makers buy wafers without competing with their supplier. Capacity expansion (Yamagata) and 200 mm qualification are the core story; a Sep 2026 300 mm substrate demo is R&D optionality, not revenue yet.
companies.street: Street leaning: Buy consensus on TSE 4004 (stockanalysis Japan coverage, 2026); US ADR coverage thin.

companies.name: ROHM
companies.role: SiCrystal substrates + captive SiC device fabs — vertical capacity.
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Listed for substrate/fab footprint; not scored on Infineon/STM device field.
companies.caveats: EV SiC demand softness; Japan ADR liquidity; conglomerate mix.
companies.rainbowReason: Impairment and BEV softness already in the narrative; not an under-priced capacity surprise.

metrics.label: Vertical (SiCrystal + fabs)
metrics.note: German SiCrystal substrates feeding captive Japan device fabs.

metrics.label: 8-inch / 200 mm shift
metrics.note: Moving to 8-inch internal substrates; external 6-inch sales downsized.

metrics.label: EV-cycle / BEV risk
metrics.note: BEV softness drove large SiC-related impairment (~¥194B).

metrics.label: Captive utilization
metrics.note: Equipment installs paused where demand soft; device lines selective full.

metrics.label: Balance sheet after impairment
metrics.note: Hit clears depreciation path to profitability targets, but confidence scar remains.

metrics.label: ADR / conglomerate mix
metrics.note: Broad analog/discrete mix; US ADR liquidity limited.

companies.thesis: ROHM owns SiCrystal substrate capacity plus captive SiC fabs — a vertical materials-to-device stack — but the investment question for this field is whether EV softness and the FY2025 impairment strand that capacity below plan. External substrate sales were cut as 6-inch oversupply hit; internal 8-inch is the recovery path.
companies.street: Street leaning: Japan sell-side mixed after SiC impairment; US ADR coverage thin (as of 2026).

companies.name: DISCO
companies.whyCapacityNotDevice: Equipment for wafer throughput, not devices and not burn-in (AEHR/Cohu).
companies.caveats: Broad semi-equipment cycle; SiC is a slice of revenue.
companies.rainbowReason: AI/HBM already prices the equipment franchise; SiC attach upside is incremental.

metrics.label: SiC wafering attach
metrics.note: Dominant share in SiC dicing/grinding tools that unlock wafer throughput.

metrics.label: 200 mm tool optionality
metrics.note: 8-inch SiC transition could refresh tool demand ~2027; not yet a boom.

metrics.label: SiC revenue purity
metrics.note: SiC remains a small slice; AI logic/HBM drive recent records.

metrics.label: Equipment cycle position
metrics.note: Broad semi-equipment cycle; SiC EV-tool demand soft in 2025–26.

metrics.label: Franchise / balance sheet
metrics.note: Cash-rich precision-equipment leader with pricing power.

metrics.label: Valuation vs peers
metrics.note: AI/HBM re-rating; SiC capacity upside not the multiple driver.

companies.thesis: DISCO sells the dicing, grinding, and polishing tools that turn SiC boules into usable wafers — a capacity enabler, not a device or burn-in name (contrast AEHR/Cohu). SiC attach share is strong, but recent profit records are AI/HBM-led; treat SiC as a call option on wafer-diameter transitions, not the core equity thesis.
companies.street: Street leaning: Buy consensus on TSE 6146 (stockanalysis / Japan coverage, 2026); SiC not the stated driver.
